title: Interleaved signal canaries and eviction policy for geo-failover and tiered-capacity deployments
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a deployment routing subsystem that supports interleaved signal-based canaries, tenant-prioritized eviction for tiered capacity pools, and deterministic geo-failover semantics when model variants show compatibility regressions. Current rollout primitives (static traffic splits + simple shadowing) are insufficient for multi-tenant workloads where capacity is limited, variants have different runtime characteristics, and region outages require deterministic, low-latency failover.

Goal: Implement a routing & fallback design that: discovers variant incompatibilities via live probes, ramps traffic with interleaved signal canaries (mixing synthetic probes and production probes), enforces a capacity-aware eviction ladder with tenant priorities, and exposes rollout telemetry and automated rollback triggers to the console and API. The system must be pluggable into existing runtime routing and respect per-customer SLAs and Dedicated capacity reservations.
acceptance_criteria: Interleaved canary controller implemented: controller schedules alternating synthetic probes and 1% production probes for new variant during canary window
Compatibility score computed in realtime per-variant: score thresholds (>=0.95) required for ramp beyond canary stage
Eviction policy implemented: capacity ladder enforces tiered preemption with tenant weights and graceful token-bucket drain to avoid tails
Geo-failover policy deterministic: region priority list + consistent hashing of sessions ensures affinity preserved when failover occurs

Auto-rollback triggers: divergence > X on output-similarity metric or P99 latency breach for 5 consecutive minutes automatically flips traffic to last-known-good variant and emits audit + debug context
Console surfaces: per-canary timeline, probe outcomes, compatibility score, and rollback reason with links to last 1k requests and sample diff logs
E2E test harness: synthetic multi-tenant workload validates ramp, eviction, and region-failover scenarios in staging
technical_notes: Compatibility scoring: combine semantic similarity (embedding-based diffs), structural validation (schema / function call adherence), and ops signals (latency, error-rate); use weighted exponential smoothing to respond to recent regressions
Interleaved canaries: canonical cadence = 45s synthetic probe -> 15s production sample batch -> repeat for 15 minutes; adjustable per-project
Eviction ladder: pools defined as reserved, burst, and shared; eviction order = burst -> shared; reserved never evicted except under admin overrides
Tenant weight model: priority = (contract_tier*2 + recent_error_budget_usage); weights normalized into eviction probability to probabilistically preserve high-priority tenants under overload

Geo-failover deterministic mapping: maintain consistent session hash namespace; when primary region unavailable, attempt ordered failover across preferred region list with KV cache warmup heuristics to reduce cold-start penalties
Rollback signatures: fingerprint last-known-good variant by (model-id, model-hash, quantization-profile, kernel-set) and store signature with warm cache snapshot for rapid reversion
Observability: emit canary_probe.{synthetic|production}.outcome, compatibility.score, eviction.reason, failover.path, rollback.trigger. Tag events with request_id and tenant_id for traceability
engineering_tasks: controller: implement canary state machine and scheduler (15d)
runtime: add probe injection hooks and sampling path for production probes (10d)
routing: implement eviction ladder + tenant-weighted preemption (8d)
metrics: compatibility scoring pipeline + realtime dashboard telemetry (5d)
console: canary timeline UI + rollback UI + links to sample diffs (6d)
e2e: staging harness for multi-region failover + tiered capacity tests (5d)
security: review auto-rollback audit trail for compliance (2d)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable canary controller in staging for non-critical models and validate compatibility score behavior with synthetic probes. Phase 2 (pilot): opt-in on 3 customers in dedicated pools, enable production probing at 0.5%-1% and observe eviction interactions. Phase 3 (gradual): enable for all hosted models with sensible defaults and per-project opt-out. Rollback policy: automatic for critical triggers + manual approval for softer signals.
risks: Production probes increase tail latency if not rate-limited; mitigate by strict sampling and circuit breakers
Eviction could violate contractual SLAs if weights misconfigured; require safety checks and manual override controls
Similarity-based rollback may trigger false positives for naturally diverse outputs; tune thresholds and combine signals
Cross-region KV cache warmup can cause higher cold starts on failover; pre-warm heuristics required
